title: BETWEEN, IN, and Pattern Matching
description: Work with range filtering via BETWEEN, list matching with IN and ANY, and advanced pattern matching with LIKE and SIMILAR TO.

data.text: SQL provides dedicated operators to simplify queries: `BETWEEN` filters across continuous ranges, `IN` filters against discrete sets of values, and `LIKE` performs pattern matching against string data.

`value BETWEEN low AND high` is shorthand for `value >= low AND value <= high`. Because it is inclusive of both boundary endpoints, be cautious when using `BETWEEN` on timestamp fields containing time components.
In PostgreSQL, filtering against an array parameter is often cleaner and faster using `= ANY($1)` rather than dynamically constructing a string of comma-separated values in an `IN (...)` clause.

data.title: Comparing IN with = ANY()
Key Takeaways
points: `BETWEEN` is inclusive on both boundaries (`>= a AND <= b`).
`IN` tests membership against a literal list or subquery result.
Use `= ANY(ARRAY[...])` in PostgreSQL when passing array parameters from application code.
